claims.head: What happened to the Canadiens’ chance quality?
claims.body: Taken over this season and last, the Canadiens are around the middle of the league for chance quality. Look at this season alone, though, and they’ve been settling for worse looks. We think tonight looks more like this season’s Canadiens.
claims.nums: Chance quality: 12th over two seasons (6.5% a shot), 20th this season (6.1% a shot)
claims.gist: The Canadiens aren’t the team you remember for chance quality.
claims.call: The Canadiens’ chance quality is worse than their blended level of 6.5% a shot.

claims.head: The Jets like Vilardi’s line against Bolduc’s
claims.call: The Jets’ L2 (Iafallo, Björck and Vilardi) spends at least 53% of its 5-on-5 time against the Canadiens’ second line.
claims.body: At home, the Jets keep sending Vilardi’s line (Iafallo, Björck and Vilardi) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Scott Arniel keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Canadiens’ second line is Bolduc, Danault and Texier.

WPG.head: Nothing to separate these two
WPG.body: Montréal has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, while Winnipeg will be without Morrissey. Then again, Winnipeg has home-ice advantage, and Montréal will be without Suzuki. For the Jets, the difference could be a penalty kill that holds up.

MTL.head: A genuine toss-up
MTL.body: Montréal has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, while Winnipeg will be without Morrissey. Then again, Winnipeg has home-ice advantage, and Montréal will be without Suzuki. The Canadiens can tip it if they keep shots to a minimum.
